summary: Publicly available sources support a hazard and contingency-policy inventory for Middlesex County, but this review did not verify facility-specific outage histories, utility dependencies, backup duration, recovery times, or contingency capacity for RWJUH (CCN 310038) or Saint Peter’s (CCN 310070). Treat the state hazard plan as contextual evidence and use an explicitly hypothetical outage scenario until hospital-specific inputs are authorized and reviewed.

sources.title: 2024 New Jersey State Hazard Mitigation Plan
sources.publisher: New Jersey Office of Emergency Management
sources.geography: New Jersey statewide; plan includes hazard and capability assessments with local-planning coordination
sources.period: 2024 plan; hazard-specific historical periods vary and require inspection of the relevant chapter
sources.grain: Narrative and tabular hazard assessments, mitigation actions, and capability information by hazard and jurisdiction where provided
useful_fields: historical occurrences and losses where reported
observed_facts: The official plan page lists hazard chapters including severe weather, severe winter weather, flood, cyber attack, and pandemic, as well as capability assessment and local-planning coordination sections.

The state plan is suitable for identifying documented hazard categories and planning context; it does not itself establish either hospital’s service-level dependencies, outage duration, or contingency capacity.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the official plan page and retrieve only relevant 2024 chapters and appendices for Middlesex County context; record the exact chapter, table, geographic scope, and source period used. Use the county hazard mitigation plan link for a separate county-level check, noting that its linked plan page returned 403 during this review.
limitations: The plan is a document, not a verified machine-readable incident dataset or hospital operational record.
County-linked plan page could not be inspected in this review, so county-specific values and download access remain unverified.
Public hazard assessments must not be used to infer hospital-specific failure likelihoods or sensitive infrastructure details.
Rights or redistribution terms were not verified on the opened plan page.

sources.title: Hazard Mitigation Plans
sources.publisher: New Jersey Office of Emergency Management
sources.grain: Index of state hazard mitigation plan versions
observed_facts: The state index says the plan captures historic disasters and current hazards, provides risk-reduction strategy, and is reviewed and submitted to FEMA at least every three years.
The index links the 2024 plan as the latest listed version.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the 2024 version linked from the index as the current statewide planning source; do not combine hazard estimates from older versions without recording their distinct period and method.
limitations: Index contains no incident-level or facility-level resilience records.
The index does not establish hospital policy authority or utility service boundaries.
Rights evidence was not found on the opened index page.

sources.title: Electric Power Annual, Table 11.2: Reliability Metrics Using IEEE of U.S. Distribution System by State
sources.geography: United States and state-level, including New Jersey
sources.period: 2023 and 2024 table shown on the opened page
sources.grain: Annual electric distribution-system reliability metrics by state
observed_facts: The EIA page labels the table as state-level reliability metrics for 2023 and 2024 and identifies Form EIA-861 as the source.
EIA notes that customer coverage is an estimate based on meters represented relative to customers reported, and can exceed 100% in some cases.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Retrieve the displayed table or the EIA-linked source files for the New Jersey row and cited reporting year; preserve metric definitions and coverage percentage alongside values. Use only as an external state-level benchmark, not a local hospital outage estimate.
limitations: Statewide utility metrics do not identify outages affecting New Brunswick or either hospital.
Annual reliability measures do not provide incident start/recovery times or hospital service-level impact.
Applicability to hospital continuity is limited; values cannot calibrate facility-specific failure likelihood without local validation.
The opened table does not establish redistribution rights for extracted data.

missing_inputs: Facility-specific outage start and recovery timestamps for RWJUH and Saint Peter’s.
Hospital service dependency inventory, including utility types and clinically important workflows; none were verified publicly in this review.
Hospital contingency policies, activation thresholds, effective dates, transfer/closure/cancellation rules, and authorized decision makers.
Backup capability and duration, affected staffed capacity, service uptime, backlog, and recovery measures by workflow.
Verified Middlesex County hazard plan tables and county incident history usable at the required disruption-by-duration grain.
Local utility-level or circuit-level reliability observations applicable to the two facilities.
simulation_use: Candidate bounded scenario: model a hypothetical external electric outage affecting a New Brunswick hospital workflow. Mark outage start time, duration, affected capacity, backlog, and recovery time as user-controlled synthetic scenario parameters; do not assign likelihoods from the sources above. Treat generator availability, fuel duration, transfer arrangements, and workflow contingency policies as unknown until independently verified by an authorized institutional owner. Use the EIA New Jersey annual metrics only as a labeled statewide contextual benchmark, not as a local probability or hospital calibration input. For policy inventory, extract only publicly documented, non-sensitive contingency authority and effective dates, and keep unverified dependencies explicitly unknown.
limitations: This is candidate research, not dataset acquisition; no source data were downloaded or normalized.
The requested exact disruption-by-duration grain and incident timestamps are not supplied by the reviewed public sources.
No local outage likelihood, hospital uptime, affected capacity, backlog, or recovery time is estimated.
Access and rights claims are limited to what was visible on the opened official pages; rights evidence was not verified for the documents or EIA table.
A Middlesex County hazard plan link was discovered but returned 403 when opened; its availability and contents remain unverified.
